name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,540

clue.text: Master with gas released big noises

indicators.note: letters that are released are set loose from their order and can fall back in any arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilled performer lets off gas, producing loud noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noises' looks like the sound of the gas, but it is the definition: the anagram of MASTER plus GAS gives MEGASTARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is an informal term for an important, famous person, which is what huge celebrities are.

clue.text: Perhaps fingers in the air meet requirements

blocks.note: a finger of whisky is one example of a drinks measure
something in the air is up

explanation.surface: Raising a finger in the air to show you meet the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fingers in the air' suggests a gesture, but fingers here are the drinks measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is to reach the standard expected, being good enough for what is needed.

clue.text: Rise and dress

blocks.note: first meaning: to get out of bed
second meaning: an outfit or costume

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a morning routine; the hyphenated noun means outfit while the verb phrase means stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up is rising from bed, and a get-up is an outfit, often an unusual one.

clue.text: Ever entered into firm with capacity to take direction?

indicators.note: something entered into another is put inside it

blocks.note: firm and stable both mean steady
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a company has ever been able to follow instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company, but it means steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A steerable vehicle can be guided, so it is capable of being pointed in a chosen course.

clue.text: Diplomat committed to seeing someone shortly

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut short and loses its final letter

blocks.note: someone in a relationship is attached

explanation.surface: An envoy is in a serious relationship and will see someone soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like soon, but it drops the last letter of ATTACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is an official on an embassy's staff, a junior member of the diplomatic service.

clue.text: Help victim of a con artist in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a sucker is a gullible person easily cheated

explanation.surface: Assistance for someone swindled, possibly at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is assistance or relief given in a time of hardship, a formal noun for aid.

clue.text: Man that must take pee in wood

indicators.note: one word must take another inside it, so the first holds the second within its letters

blocks.note: a man is a male
pee is the spoken name of the letter P

explanation.surface: A man needs to relieve himself in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits in the surface as part of the scene; the container is signalled by 'must take', with MALE holding P to give MAPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a kind of tree whose timber is a familiar furniture and flooring wood.

clue.text: They smuggle another's drugs in shoes

blocks.note: first meaning: couriers who carry narcotics for a dealer
second meaning: backless slippers

explanation.surface: Couriers hide narcotics in their footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug couriers are known as mules, and mules are also backless slip-on shoes or slippers.

clue.text: I paint car in a slap-dash way for aristocrat

indicators.note: work done carelessly is jumbled, so the letters come out in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sloppy spray job on a toff's motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of Rome's noble class, and the word now means any person of high birth.

clue.text: On occasion, lairy dons dished the dirt

indicators.note: on occasion means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is used
dished means ruined or spoilt, so the word that follows is wrecked and rearranged
to don is to put on clothing, so one set of letters wears the other around it

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of lairy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Brash academics spread scandalous gossip now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished the dirt' reads as one idiom, but it splits into an anagram signal, its fodder and the definition. Lairy is British slang for flashy or aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth and dirt both mean soil, the loose ground material that plants grow in.

clue.text: Proper tune I chat about

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so the letters are turned around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes chatting about a respectable, decent song.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper can mean real or genuine, the sense in which something is authentic rather than fake.

clue.text: In a bit of fluster after horse bolts

indicators.note: a horse that bolts runs off, so that letter runs off and leaves the word

blocks.note: to be in a lather is to be flustered and agitated
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone gets flustered when a horse runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: LATHER loses its H to leave LATER. Horse as slang for heroin, shortened to H, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and in a bit both mean at some time soon after now, so the adverb phrases are interchangeable.

clue.text: Superior evening meal son polished off

indicators.note: something polished off is finished and got rid of, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: supper is a meal eaten in the evening
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A posh dinner which the son wolfed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polished off' suggests eating up the meal, but it removes the S from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank or status, as in the upper classes, matching superior.

clue.text: Quite angry about female star of The Deep?

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer letters wrap round the one inside

blocks.note: cross is angry, and the suffix -ish means quite or somewhat
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A cross actress who starred in a film called The Deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -ish means somewhat. The Deep looks like a film title, but here it is the sea, whose star is a starfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfish is an old regional name for the starfish, a creature shaped like a star living in the sea.

clue.text: Pretty flirty cow might do this, I'm told

indicators.note: what I am told is heard rather than read, so the phrase is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a flirtatious cow would ogle a bull

explanation.surface: A pretty, coquettish cow giving someone the glad eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeable is a rare word for something pleasant to look at, so attractive or good-looking.

clue.text: Use less MDMA? Come on, silly, one's consumed by it!

indicators.note: silly means foolish and confused, so the letters are muddled into another order
something consumed by another is swallowed inside it

blocks.note: MDMA is the drug ecstasy, known as E
taken as written
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A clubber is urged to cut down on ecstasy, being hooked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: E starts the answer; IS goes into COME ON and the whole lot is rearranged. Ecstasy is often called E.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to cut back spending or consumption, the intransitive sense of using less.

clue.text: Pressure to split up old sort and a model

indicators.note: a letter that splits a word goes into its middle, breaking it into two parts

blocks.note: a relic can be an old-fashioned person
P is the physics symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pressure is being used to break up an elderly couple and a model.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside RELIC to give REPLIC, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, and a model can be a scaled copy of something.

clue.text: Another pagan term?

indicators.note: another version of the words is a different form of them, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the star symbol is itself a term heavily associated with paganism.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star used as a symbol in pagan and occult religion, so it is fairly called a pagan term.

clue.text: Spongy dessert knight tucks into after sailor

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to get inside it, so that letter goes within the word

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
sorbet is a frozen fruit dessert
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight eats a pudding after a sailor has had his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' looks like eating, but it signals an insertion. N for knight comes from chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent soaks up liquid readily, which is exactly what a sponge does.

clue.text: Ace part of speech produces memorable phrase

blocks.note: an ace is an expert, a pro
a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech

explanation.surface: A brilliant bit of talk leads to a quotable line.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short, well-known saying, the kind of pithy phrase people remember and repeat.

clue.text: Drink following party - that's a mistake

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first item named is placed second

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance party
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Having a drink after a party proves a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls-up is British slang for a bungled job.
explanation.definitionFit: A balls-up is a vulgar British term for a muddle or blunder, something badly botched.

clue.text: Fruit bats

blocks.note: first meaning: the long yellow fruits
second meaning: crazy, as in batty

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fruit bats, the animals; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the tropical yellow fruit in the plural, and as slang it is an adjective meaning crazy or mad.

clue.text: I am heading to soirée wearing straw hat

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used
something worn is inside the garment, so the hat wraps round that letter

blocks.note: a boater is a stiff straw hat
the first letter of soirée

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are off to an evening party in a straw hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'I am' is the phrase a braggart keeps saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster talks endlessly about himself, so 'I am' sums up his brag-filled speech.

clue.text: Mafioso cut down in wicked vendetta's finale

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the very end of the word is kept

blocks.note: wicked is slang for excellent, so good
to fell is to cut down a tree
the final letter of vendetta

explanation.surface: A gangster is gunned down in a feud ending in violence.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked as slang praise is the opposite of its surface sense of evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodfella is American slang for a gangster in the Mafia, popularised by the film Goodfellas.

clue.text: Good girl? Crystal could be one!

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a girl named Crystal is a well-behaved one.
explanation.walkthrough: Crystal looks like a girl's name, but it is high-quality glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is a fine, clear kind of glass, so it is an example of that material.

clue.text: Fellow with impotent lover

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
lame means weak or ineffectual

explanation.surface: A man with a lover who cannot perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame, as in an old flame, is a sweetheart or romantic partner.

clue.text: Hate violent crime associated with men

blocks.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a criminal assault charge in Britain
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone loathes violent crime committed by men.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British assault offence; OR for men is the military other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe something intensely, the verb hate used strongly.

clue.text: Homework at inferior Karachi uni initially takes little work

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Assignments at a second-rate Pakistani university require little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a very short Japanese poem of three lines, so a small literary piece.

clue.text: Woman I married shows spirit

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the letters are on view inside the words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of Woman, all of I and the start of married

explanation.surface: A man says the woman he wed is full of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The words look like a charade of a name plus I and M, but the letters are simply sitting in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Anima is the soul or inner life force, and in Jung's psychology the feminine side of the psyche.

clue.text: Miserable function a performer gate-crashes

indicators.note: a gate-crasher pushes into a party uninvited, so these letters force their way inside the others

blocks.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a turn is a variety act or performer

explanation.surface: An entertainer barges into a party, making it a gloomy do.
explanation.walkthrough: Function looks like a social event, but it is the maths function sine, split open by A TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, supposedly caused by the planet Saturn's influence.

clue.text: Head for New Zealand with Scandinavian

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for the head, used in New Zealand and Australia
second meaning

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for New Zealand with a Scandinavian companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head for' reads as a verb of travel, but Head is a noun here, and a swede is also a turnip-like root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Swede is antipodean slang for the head, like nut or noggin, and it is also a native of Sweden.

clue.text: Most important horse soldier at the front

indicators.note: at the front says which piece leads, so the second item named comes first

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A cavalryman leading from the front is the chief figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse soldier' looks like a cavalryman, but 'at the front' puts the soldier ahead of the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of the highest importance, above all other considerations.
